## Effects

_Psychic_ deals damage and has a 10% chance of lowering the target's Special Defense by one stage.

Stats can be lowered to a minimum of -6 stages each.

### Changes

*   In Generation 1, _Psychic_ has a 30% chance of lowering the target's Special stat (Sp.Atk and Sp.Def combined).  

### Z-Move effects

When a Pokémon is holding [Psychium Z](https://www.pokemondb.net/item/psychium-z) and uses its Z-Power, _Psychic_ turns into [Shattered Psyche](https://www.pokemondb.net/move/shattered-psyche) and has base power **175**.

When Mew is holding [Mewnium Z](https://www.pokemondb.net/item/mewnium-z) and uses its Z-Power, _Psychic_ turns into [Genesis Supernova](https://www.pokemondb.net/move/genesis-supernova) and has base power **185**.

## Effects

_Psychic_ deals damage and has a 10% chance of lowering the target's Special Defense by one stage.

Stats can be lowered to a minimum of -6 stages each.

### Changes

*   In Generation 1, _Psychic_ has a 30% chance of lowering the target's Special stat (Sp.Atk and Sp.Def combined).  

### Z-Move effects

When a Pokémon is holding [Psychium Z](https://www.pokemondb.net/item/psychium-z) and uses its Z-Power, _Psychic_ turns into [Shattered Psyche](https://www.pokemondb.net/move/shattered-psyche) and has base power **175**.

When Mew is holding [Mewnium Z](https://www.pokemondb.net/item/mewnium-z) and uses its Z-Power, _Psychic_ turns into [Genesis Supernova](https://www.pokemondb.net/move/genesis-supernova) and has base power **185**.

Psychic (Japanese: サイコキネシス Psychokinesis) is a damage-dealing Psychic-type move introduced in Generation I.

It is:

TM29 from Generation I to Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon, and in Pokémon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl.
TM40 in Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!.
TR11 in Pokémon Sword and Shield.
TM120 in Pokémon Scarlet and Violet.
TM063 in Pokémon Legends: Z-A.

It can be upgraded to the special Z-Move Genesis Supernova by Mew holding Mewnium Z.

Effect
Generation I

Psychic does damage and has a 33.2% chance of lowering the target's Special by one stage.

When used by an in-game opponent, there is an additional chance of 25% for the effect to fail (resulting in an effective chance of 24.9%).

Generation II

Psychic now has a 10% chance of lowering the target's Special Defense by one stage.

When used by an in-game opponent, there is still an additional chance of 25% for the effect to fail (resulting in an effective chance of 7.5%). This does not apply when Lock-On or Mind Reader are in effect, nor in the Battle Tower.

Generation III onwards

Psychic's effect no longer has an additional chance to fail when used by an in-game opponent.

Psychic can be used as the first move of a Pokémon Contest combination, causing Confusion, Future Sight, Kinesis, and Teleport to score double the normal appeal if used in the next turn. It can also be used to finish a combination, with the user gaining 1 bonus appeal point if Calm Mind, Confusion, or Kinesis was used in the previous turn.

Psychic (Japanese: サイコキネシス Psychokinesis) is a damage-dealing Psychic-type move introduced in Generation I.

It is:

TM29 from Generation I to Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon, and in Pokémon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl.
TM40 in Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!.
TR11 in Pokémon Sword and Shield.
TM120 in Pokémon Scarlet and Violet.
TM063 in Pokémon Legends: Z-A.

It can be upgraded to the special Z-Move Genesis Supernova by Mew holding Mewnium Z.

Effect
Generation I

Psychic does damage and has a 33.2% chance of lowering the target's Special by one stage.

When used by an in-game opponent, there is an additional chance of 25% for the effect to fail (resulting in an effective chance of 24.9%).

Generation II

Psychic now has a 10% chance of lowering the target's Special Defense by one stage.

When used by an in-game opponent, there is still an additional chance of 25% for the effect to fail (resulting in an effective chance of 7.5%). This does not apply when Lock-On or Mind Reader are in effect, nor in the Battle Tower.

Generation III onwards

Psychic's effect no longer has an additional chance to fail when used by an in-game opponent.

Psychic can be used as the first move of a Pokémon Contest combination, causing Confusion, Future Sight, Kinesis, and Teleport to score double the normal appeal if used in the next turn. It can also be used to finish a combination, with the user gaining 1 bonus appeal point if Calm Mind, Confusion, or Kinesis was used in the previous turn.

# Red/Blue Gym Leaders & Elite Four

The standard Pokémon format as initialised here in Red/Blue is to battle your way through 8 gyms, each specializing in a particular type. Following that you take on the Elite Four and the Champion.

### Gym Leaders

1.   Brock(Pewter City)
2.   Misty(Cerulean City)
3.   Lt. Surge(Vermilion City)
4.   Erika(Celadon City)
5.   Koga(Fuchsia City)
6.   Sabrina(Saffron City)
7.   Blaine(Cinnabar Island)
8.   Giovanni(Viridian City)

### Elite Four

1.   Lorelei
2.   Bruno
3.   Agatha
4.   Lance
5.   Blue

# Red/Blue Gym Leaders & Elite Four

The standard Pokémon format as initialised here in Red/Blue is to battle your way through 8 gyms, each specializing in a particular type. Following that you take on the Elite Four and the Champion.

### Gym Leaders

1.   Brock(Pewter City)
2.   Misty(Cerulean City)
3.   Lt. Surge(Vermilion City)
4.   Erika(Celadon City)
5.   Koga(Fuchsia City)
6.   Sabrina(Saffron City)
7.   Blaine(Cinnabar Island)
8.   Giovanni(Viridian City)

### Elite Four

1.   Lorelei
2.   Bruno
3.   Agatha
4.   Lance
5.   Blue
